Why Flexibility Matters in Nail Adhesives
summary: Learn how adhesive flexibility impacts press-on nail comfort, wear, and removal—and how H.B. Fuller Beauty delivers performance-driven solutions for every brand.
body_text: When it comes to press-on nails, consumers want it all: salon-quality hold, comfortable wear, and safe removal. Behind every successful press-on system lies an invisible hero — the adhesive. At H.B. Fuller Beauty, we formulate solutions that meet the wear expectations of every brand. One of the most important performance characteristics in press-on adhesives is flexibility. The Science of Flexibility Cyanoacrylate adhesives - the backbone of most nail glues - cure into a thin polymer film that bonds the artificial nail to the natural nail plate. The flexibility of this bond depends on the cyanoacrylate’s side chain chemistry: Ethyl Cyanoacrylate forms a firm, fast-setting bond with strong initial grab — ideal for consumers who prefer a secure, “salon-style” feel. Ethoxyethyl Cyanoacrylate offers enhanced flexibility, allowing the bond to move more naturally with the nail. Both chemistries deliver strong adhesion; the difference lies in the type of wear experience your brand wants to offer. Why Flexibility Matters for Nails Comfort in Daily Life Nails flex during everyday activities like typing, cooking, or opening packaging. Adhesives with higher flexibility can follow this movement, while firmer bonds give consumers that crisp, ultra-secure feel they associate with salon systems. Wear Performance and Retention Firmer bonds provide immediate, confident hold. More flexible bonds help distribute stress across the nail, supporting long-lasting wear even under dynamic movement. Nail Health and Removal Experience Nail options matter. Some brands prioritize a “professional-strength” hold, while others focus on gentle removal and reduced brittleness. Flexibility and rigidity each support different consumer expectations. Consumer Confidence Whether the goal is a salon-strong hold or a flexible, natural-feel wear, the right chemistry helps consumers trust the system — driving repeat use and brand loyalty. How H.B. Fuller Beauty Leads with Flexibility Our Essential Series is designed to give beauty brands performance choice - without compromise. Essential Classic (Ethyl) → Fast-setting, firm, professional-strength bond ideal for consumers who want a crisp, confident, salon-style feel. Essential Gentle (Ethoxyethyl) → Flexible, low-odor, nail-friendly formula designed for brands prioritizing comfort, natural flex, and easy removal. Both options deliver high-performance adhesion. Bond With Confidence Flexibility isn’t just a technical feature — it’s one of the keys to balancing adhesion strength, comfort, and nail wellness. At H.B. title: Introducing Stop-Loss Reporting Automation - Amera - AI-Powered Claims Processing Automation for Healthcare
summary: With Amera, TPAs can instantly report claims when they exceed stop-loss limits, enabling faster recovery and better patient outcomes
body_text: Currently TPAs manually generate reports when claims surpass stop-loss limits. This requires a ton of manual effort to assemble the relevant data and documents. Meanwhile, stop-loss providers wait weeks before they can start evaluating these claims, leading to worse economic and patient outcomes. With Amera, TPAs can instantly ingest carrier contracts, identify relevant claims, enrich with case management and PBM data, and show exactly what documentation is needed for submission, all without an extra team of people who could be working on more valuable activities. Amera ingests the stop-loss contract, continuously monitors claims activity, and tells the TPA team: Which members are approaching or exceeding the deductible (with diagnosis, Rx, and case management context) What’s eligible for reimbursement and the exact documentation required How the plan is tracking toward the aggregate attachment point (claims, enrollment, lag validation) Which claimants and drugs are likely to drive lasers and renewal risk We’re seeing teams go from weeks of back-and-forth and document chasing to having everything ready for submission in seconds with fewer carrier rejections and faster recovery. Results: Recovery time reduced from 2+ weeks to seconds, fewer carrier rejections, and a team focused on complex cases instead of data compilation
